subject: Request: VM cadence & signed SLA attestation for FinTrust SIG response
messages:
From: Paul Nguyen <p.nguyen@fintrust.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Cc: security@fintrust.com
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: VM cadence and SLA evidence for SIG/CAIQ

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our SIG/CAIQ update we need specific vulnerability management evidence for Redwood. Can you confirm the following in writing:

- Scan cadence (authenticated/full, unauthenticated/light) and tooling used.
- SLA targets for remediation by severity (Critical/High/Medium/Low).
- Time-to-detect and time-to-remediate averages for the last 90 days (or an explanation if aggregated reporting is not available).
- Process for emergency/zero-day CVEs and any escalation path we can rely on.
- Retention window for scan artifacts and proof-of-remediation evidence.

We also need a signed attestation on company letterhead that the SLA commitments above are accurate for inclusion in our SIG submission. Ideally we can have the attestation by EOD Thursday (2027-03-04).

If you can send the disclosures and attach the recent scan export, that would help us close the questionnaire quickly.

Best,
Paul
Paul Nguyen
Security Operations
FinTrust Payments

[Attachment requested: scan export, signed SLA attestation]

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
To: Paul Nguyen <p.nguyen@fintrust.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: VM cadence and SLA evidence for SIG/CAIQ

Hi Paul — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; Jonas and Monica are looped to provide the artifacts and a signed attestation following review.

Summary commitments (we will provide a signed letter and artifact package):
- Scanning cadence: weekly full authenticated scans across all production subnets; daily lightweight unauthenticated scans targeting internet-exposed endpoints. Ad-hoc targeted scans run after any infra change or onboarding of new service.
- Tooling: commercial Nessus/Tenable for authenticated vulnerability enumeration + internal host-based scanners for container images and OS baselines. Results are ingested into our tracker for prioritization.
- SLA remediation targets (standard): Critical: 7 calendar days (or faster with active mitigation); High: 30 days; Medium: 90 days; Low: regular maintenance window. We have an emergency triage track for active exploitation.
- Zero-day response: initial triage within 24 hours, mitigation plan within 72 hours, escalation to our on-call infra and product owners. If a workaround is required, we document compensating controls and timelines in the ticket.
- Evidence retention: raw scan exports and remediation proofs retained 365 days for SOC/SIG requests; executive summaries retained longer.

Deliverables and timeline:
- Technical scan export (CSV) and executive summary PDF: by tomorrow morning.
- Draft attestation letter for your review: tomorrow afternoon.
- Signed attestation (PDF or DocuSign): EOD Thu (2027-03-04).

If you need us to reference specific CAIQ question IDs, send the item numbers and we'll annotate the attestation.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Trust & Security Programs
Redwood Inference

--

Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: VM cadence and SLA evidence for SIG/CAIQ — scan exports attached

Paul — attaching the requested artifacts and a short technical note on our process. See attachments: scan-summary-20270228.csv, redwood_vm_evidence_q1_2027.pdf (executive scan summary).

Technical note (abridged):
- Authenticated weekly scans execute across all reachable instances with credentialed Nessus policies; we supplement with container image CVE scans on CI.
- Scheduled daily unauthenticated discovery scans target external subnets to catch public-facing regressions between full scans.
- Mean time to detect (MTTD) from our telemetry (last 90 days): 12 hours for externally-exposed high/critical findings; internal detections vary by agent heartbeat.
- Mean time to remediate (MTTR) metrics (rolling 90-day): Critical: 4.8 days (median 3.1), High: 18 days, Medium: 51 days. We will include CSV slices for your ingestion.
- Emergency process: exploitation indicators triaged to Severity Response Team; if immediate patching is not possible we deploy compensating WAF rules or host-level mitigations and escalate to infra-on-call.
- Exceptions: we maintain documented exception tickets for scenarios requiring longer patch windows; these are reviewed weekly by risk ops.
- Retention: full scan exports, patch tickets, and remediation evidence are stored in our secure drive for 365 days; we can export evidence packages on request.

Attachments: 1) scan-summary-20270228.csv (filtered export) 2) redwood_vm_evidence_q1_2027.pdf (executive summary)

Let us know if the CSV needs different columns for your ingestion.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Director, Platform Security
Redwood Inference

Lauren/Jonas — thanks for the quick turnaround and the artifacts. The CSV and PDF look good on a first pass. For the SIG submission we need a signed attestation that explicitly references the SLA targets and retention policy you outlined (Critical 7d, High 30d, retention 365d).

2) a DocuSign envelope we can accept programmatically into our compliance system.

Can you indicate which option you prefer and when we can expect the signed artifact? We are targeting submission on Friday, so EOD Thu is realistic but earlier is better.

Appreciate it — Paul
